name: travel-walk-v1
status: draft: defaults from research, not yet reviewed by the author
audience: one person planning a city break who wants to feel the place before going
_doc: Pixel units: `canvas.width/height` are output pixels (2160x3840 by default, the author's preference since 2026-10-11). Every other pixel number in this file (safe_zone, overlay_positions, typography.*.size, animation.in.distance_px) and in overlays/src/presets.ts and slots.json is in a 1080-wide reference space (`canvas.reference_width`), so the numbers read as on a 1080x1920 frame. Canvas pixels = reference pixels x canvas.width / canvas.reference_width (x2 at 2160x3840). The overlay renderer (overlays/src/style.ts designScale) and cf.canvas (Python) apply that one factor. Named canvases: `canvases` holds one preset per orientation (portrait, landscape), each with its own size, reference_width and, where they differ from the top-level ones, safe_zone, overlay_positions and slots (all in that preset's reference space). `canvas` is the active default (portrait); a Script's top-level `canvas` ('landscape') picks a preset, and `--canvas landscape|portrait|WxH` on cf.build / cf.render / cf.render_check / overlays/render.mjs wins over both.

canvas.note: Active default canvas (= canvases.portrait): 4K vertical (author, 2026-10-11). cf.build/cf.render take --canvas 1080x1920 for comparison renders, --canvas landscape (or a Script's canvas: 'landscape') for 16:9.

canvases._doc: Named canvas presets (cf.canvas.resolve, overlays/render.mjs). A preset without safe_zone / overlay_positions / slots uses the top-level ones (style.json safe_zone, overlay_positions, overlays/src/slots.json). A preset with overlay_positions has role_placement 'overlay_positions': every overlay preset (presets.ts) takes its anchor/x/y from there instead of its own portrait placement; font sizes, boxes and caps stay, so text is the same size relative to the frame's short side (designScale = width / reference_width = 2 on both 4K canvases). A WxH override picks the preset with the same aspect ratio.

portrait.note: 9:16 Reel; safe_zone, overlay_positions and slots are the top-level ones (Meta Reels UI).

landscape.note: 16:9 for YouTube and the Instagram feed (first horizontal video: reel-02-boat, 2026-10-11). Reference space 1920x1080, x2 at 3840x2160.

safe_zone.source: 5 % margins all round (title-safe for 16:9); bottom 12 % keeps text clear of the YouTube progress bar and player controls. No right rail: feed and YouTube put no buttons over a 16:9 frame.

slots._doc: Named placements for a spec's `anchor` on this canvas (same names as overlays/src/slots.json, 1920x1080 reference px). bottom-* y is the box's bottom edge at rest; the 24 px slide-in starts below it, so y <= 1080 - 130 - 24 = 926.

lower-left-loose._note: inside the 5 % frame margin but over the YouTube controls band (safe-zone warning); for the Instagram feed only

safe_zone.source: Meta Ads Guide 14% / 35% / 6% as relayed in docs/research/02-overlays-and-motion-graphics/result-a.md Section D

typography.preset_note: overlay design system from overlays/src/presets.ts: legacy | editorial-serif | clean-grotesk | lower-third-tag | tiktok-hype | pinterest-aesthetic | coquette-girly | y2k-gloss | diary-typewriter | handwritten-note. Non-legacy presets override display/body, colors.text/backdrop and overlay_positions for overlays. Board: reels/reel-01/overlay-design/board.png

look.brief: rich, saturated, expensive cinematic travel-film image: deep but not crushed shadows, glowing highlights, warm/teal split, skin protected

speech.note: the author films and talks from behind the camera; that is fine (music covers it). Only the person ON camera talking is a reject, until the voiceover phase.

ending.note: every Reel loops: the last shot and the first shot are one continuous action from one clip, split at the seam (author rule, 2026-10-10)

upscale.mode_note: '2x' since 2026-10-11: on reel-01 (4 of 8 shots upscaled) '2x-enhanced' rendered in 314 s vs 47 s for plain 2x, 27 s without Super Scale and 10 s at 1080x1920, over the ~5x budget. sharpness / noise_reduction are only used by '2x-enhanced'. Comparison: reels/reel-01/out/superscale-compare.png in the potsdam-2026-10-04 Walk.
upscale.note: Resolve Studio Super Scale on every source clip whose display height is below canvas.height (the 1080x1920 iPhone clips on a 2160x3840 canvas); clips at or above it get 1 (off). mode '2x-enhanced' = SetClipProperty('Super Scale', 2, sharpness, noise_reduction) with floats 0..1; mode '2x' = SetClipProperty('Super Scale', 2). cf.build --no-superscale sets every clip to 1.

reframe.note: How a landscape clip fills the vertical canvas when a shot has no reframe (cf.reframe): 'follow' = a static 9:16 window on the person (cf.follow: person detector on the proxy, the window that holds the whole person in the most frames, ties toward the end of the shot; never leaves the source, no Tilt). 'smart' (Resolve Smart Reframe) is available per shot but off by default: it tilts past the source edge and leaves black bands (Mallorca reel-01: 692 and 644 px; author: black bars are unacceptable, 2026-10-11).

render.codec_note: H.264 High is the default (Instagram re-encodes everything). GetRenderCodecs('mp4') on this Mac also lists 'H265' (H.265), which would give a smaller file at the same quality; not used, because render_check and the loudness fix expect h264.
render.bitrate_note: VideoQuality cap per canvas (SetRenderSettings VideoQuality = Mbit/s x 1000, kbit/s).
